test_title: PYST 40: SSC CHSL 2023 - English (Held On: 17 Aug, 2023 Shift 4)
subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

A owl was / hooting throughout / the night.
solution:
The correct answer is '1'' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The article 'A' before a vowel sound is incorrect. It should be 'An'.
 
• The word **'owl'** begins with a vowel sound, making the use of **'An'** necessary for correct grammar.
 
• Articles are used before nouns to define whether something is specific or not. Here, the correct indefinite article before a vowel sound is **'An'**.
 
• The error in the sentence is due to the incorrect use of the article. Therefore, 'A owl was' should be corrected to 'An owl was'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: ***An owl was** hooting throughout the night*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The rest of the sentence, **'hooting throughout'** and **'the night'**, do not contain grammatical errors and are correctly constructed.
 
• Option 'No error' is not correct because there is a grammatical mistake in the use of the article before 'owl'.
 
• Understanding the use of articles is crucial in English for both speaking and writing, as it helps clarify whether we’re referring to something specific or nonspecific.
 
• Articles 'a', 'an', and 'the' are some of the most common words in English, yet they require careful consideration to use correctly.
